newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA UNLEADED GAS SALES SLOW, PRICE MOVE URGED.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA UNLEADED GAS SALES SLOW, PRICE MOVE URGED.

text.p: The price differential between leaded and unleaded gasoline had to be increased to boost stagnant sales, South African Petroleum Industry Association director Colin McClelland said on Monday.
He said in the association's latest annual report that unleaded gasoline, introduced since February last year, now accounted for about nine percent of total gasoline sales.
"Penetration has stagnated at this level and there is now a need for an increased price differential to reach the targeted 20 percent penetration," he said.
Sapia initially asked the government for a five percent discount on unleaded gasoline, or about 10 cents, but the government only agreed to a four cent differential.
McClelland said that the industry had invested about 300 million rand in infrastructure to support the introduction of unleaded gasoline.
Unleaded South African gas currently costs 210 cents a litre.
